per_pair.why: Tighter frame spacing in acceleration/deceleration creates more snappy, responsive feel.
Sharp direction changes with clear red movement indicators feel instantly responsive versus gradual turns.
Crisp blue afterimage trails and pixel-perfect corner execution demonstrate superior dash responsiveness.

loser_biggest_gap: Add visual feedback indicators (movement direction lines, dash trails) to clarify intent and responsiveness—Game A's movement is smooth but lacks the immediate feedback that makes Game B feel reactive.
loser_other_gaps: Tighten animation frame spacing to reduce perceived sluggishness in starts and stops
Sharpen corner rounding and direction-change responsiveness—current turns feel too gradual
Improve backdrop contrast to make character silhouette more readable during movement
reasoning: Game B achieves tighter, more responsive movement through consistent frame timing, clear visual feedback via directional indicators and trails, and snappy direction changes. Game A's movement is smooth and well-spaced but lacks the immediate, reactive feel of a polished indie standard. The visual feedback gap is especially pronounced—B's red indicators and crisp trails signal movement intent instantly, while A requires the player to infer responsiveness from pose alone.
